target_customer: Companies and developers running AI agents that need API access without exposing credentials
problem: Agents given real API keys can leak or misuse them; OneCLI keeps keys in a gateway, applies per-agent policy and logs every call.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) self-hosted core with a paid cloud
product_category: AI agent credential gateway and vault

founders.name: Jonathan Fishner
prior_employers: Axis Security (zero trust network access, acquired by HPE)

founders.name: Guy Ben Aharon
prior_employers: Argon (first employee, acquired by Aqua Security)

competitors.name: HashiCorp Vault
competitors.what: Infrastructure secrets manager; OneCLI positions itself as complementary

competitors.name: Infisical Agent Vault
competitors.what: Agent-facing broker from a secrets management platform

technical_complexity.rationale: A proxy gateway that swaps placeholder keys on outbound requests, with policy and logging; standard security engineering with some hard parts around trust.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and integrations with sandboxes and tools help adoption, but vault vendors can add the same feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bitwarden announced an integration with OneCLI in April 2026 per a launch summary; no copy documented.

market_need_then: Agent sandboxes proliferated in 2026 and the company cites developers putting live keys such as Stripe keys into agents; adoption claims of 2.5K GitHub stars come from aggregators.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, tagline The vault for agents

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repo adopted by NanoClaw and featured on Hacker News as a Show HN, per aggregator summaries.

brand_strength.rationale: Some developer community pull, but the name collides with Lenovo XClarity Essentials OneCLI, which dominates search results.

outcome_analysis: OneCLI is a Summer 2026 YC company with no outcome yet. Open source distribution and a timely agent security need give it early developer traction, while vault incumbents and a name that collides with a Lenovo product are risks.
notes: Caplight says $500K with YC lead; Dealroom says $125k seed; both unverified aggregators and consistent with the YC standard deal, so no round recorded.
